title.sl: Vsi načini prihodnosti: will, going to, leaves
title.de: Alle Arten der Zukunft: will, going to, leaves
title.it: Tutti i modi del futuro: will, going to, leaves
title.en: It'll rain, the bus leaves at nine

goal.sl: Izbereš pravi način za prihodnost (I think it'll rain, It's going to rain, The bus leaves at nine) in poveš, kaj bo ob nekem času v teku (This time tomorrow I'll be walking).
goal.de: Du wählst die richtige Art für die Zukunft (I think it'll rain, It's going to rain, The bus leaves at nine) und sagst, was zu einer Zeit gerade läuft (This time tomorrow I'll be walking).
goal.it: Scegli il modo giusto per il futuro (I think it'll rain, It's going to rain, The bus leaves at nine) e dici ciò che a una certa ora sarà in corso (This time tomorrow I'll be walking).
goal.en: You can choose the right way to talk about the future (I think it'll rain, It's going to rain, The bus leaves at nine) and say what will be going on at a time (This time tomorrow I'll be walking).

say.sl: **It'll rain** ali **It's going to rain**? Kar misliš: **I think it'll rain.** (Mislim, da bo deževalo.) **I don't think he'll come.** Kar se že vidi: **Look at those clouds! It's going to rain.** (Poglej te oblake, deževalo bo.) Pogosto je oboje prav.
say.de: **It'll rain** oder **It's going to rain**? Was du meinst: **I think it'll rain.** (Ich glaube, es wird regnen.) **I don't think he'll come.** Was man schon sieht: **Look at those clouds! It's going to rain.** (Schau dir die Wolken an, es wird gleich regnen.) Oft geht beides.
say.it: **It'll rain** o **It's going to rain**? Ciò che pensi: **I think it'll rain.** (Credo che pioverà.) **I don't think he'll come.** Ciò che si vede già: **Look at those clouds! It's going to rain.** (Guarda quelle nuvole, sta per piovere.) Spesso vanno bene tutti e due.
say.en: **It'll rain** or **It's going to rain**? What you think: **I think it'll rain.** **I don't think he'll come.** What you can already see: **Look at those clouds! It's going to rain.** Often both are right.

examples.de: Ich glaube nicht, dass er kommt.

examples.en: Look at those clouds! It's going to rain.
examples.de: Schau dir die Wolken an! Es wird gleich regnen.
examples.it: Guarda quelle nuvole! Sta per piovere.

say.sl: **The bus leaves at nine**: sedanjik za to, kar piše v voznem redu ali na urniku. (Avtobus odpelje ob devetih.) **The market opens at eight.** **What time does the train get in?** Tudi **The bus will leave at nine** je prav, a redkeje. Za tvoj načrt sedanjik ne gre: **I'm going to walk.**
say.de: **The bus leaves at nine**: das Präsens für das, was im Fahrplan oder im Programm steht. (Der Bus fährt um neun.) **The market opens at eight.** **What time does the train get in?** Auch **The bus will leave at nine** stimmt, ist aber seltener. Für deinen Plan geht das Präsens nicht: **I'm going to walk.**
say.it: **The bus leaves at nine**: il presente per ciò che dice l'orario o il programma. (L'autobus parte alle nove.) **The market opens at eight.** **What time does the train get in?** Anche **The bus will leave at nine** è giusto, ma è più raro. Per un tuo programma il presente non va: **I'm going to walk.**
say.en: **The bus leaves at nine**: the present for what a timetable or a programme says. **The market opens at eight.** **What time does the train get in?** **The bus will leave at nine** is right too, but rarer. For your own plan the present won't do: **I'm going to walk.**

say.sl: **I'm seeing the doctor on Friday**: kar je dogovorjeno z nekom, gre v sedanjik z -ing. (V petek grem k zdravniku.) Načrt: **We're going to climb Helvellyn.** Odločiš se zdaj, ponudiš, obljubiš: **I'll help you.** To poznaš iz A2.
say.de: **I'm seeing the doctor on Friday**: Was mit jemandem ausgemacht ist, steht im Präsens mit -ing. (Am Freitag gehe ich zum Arzt.) Ein Plan: **We're going to climb Helvellyn.** Jetzt beschlossen, angeboten, versprochen: **I'll help you.** Das kennst du von A2.
say.it: **I'm seeing the doctor on Friday**: ciò che è fissato con qualcuno va al presente con -ing. (Venerdì vado dal medico.) Un programma: **We're going to climb Helvellyn.** Decidi adesso, offri, prometti: **I'll help you.** Lo conosci dall'A2.
say.en: **I'm seeing the doctor on Friday**: what is arranged with someone takes the present with -ing. A plan: **We're going to climb Helvellyn.** You decide now, offer or promise: **I'll help you.** You know these from A2.

examples.en: I'm seeing the doctor on Friday.

say.sl: **This time tomorrow I'll be walking on Helvellyn**: **will be** + -ing za to, kar bo ob nekem času v teku. (Jutri ob tem času bom hodil{m:|f:a} po Helvellynu.) **At eight we'll be having breakfast.** Zanikano: **I won't be working on Sunday.** (V nedeljo ne bom delal{m:|f:a}.)
say.de: **This time tomorrow I'll be walking on Helvellyn**: **will be** + -ing für das, was zu einer Zeit gerade läuft. (Morgen um diese Zeit bin ich am Helvellyn unterwegs.) **At eight we'll be having breakfast.** Verneint: **I won't be working on Sunday.** (Am Sonntag arbeite ich nicht.)
say.it: **This time tomorrow I'll be walking on Helvellyn**: **will be** + -ing per ciò che a una certa ora sarà in corso. (Domani a quest'ora camminerò sull'Helvellyn.) **At eight we'll be having breakfast.** Negativo: **I won't be working on Sunday.** (Domenica non lavoro.)
say.en: **This time tomorrow I'll be walking on Helvellyn**: **will be** + -ing for what will be going on at a time. **At eight we'll be having breakfast.** No: **I won't be working on Sunday.**

say.sl: **Will you be using the van tomorrow?** Vljudno vprašanje o načrtih: ne prosiš še, samo sprašuješ. (Boš jutri rabil{m:|f:a} kombi?) Kar bo tako ali tako: **I'll be seeing Jack at the market, so I can tell him.** (Jacka bom tako ali tako videl{m:|f:a} na tržnici, pa mu lahko povem.)
say.de: **Will you be using the van tomorrow?** Höflich nach Plänen fragen: Du bittest noch nicht, du fragst nur. (Brauchst du morgen den Lieferwagen?) Was sowieso geschieht: **I'll be seeing Jack at the market, so I can tell him.** (Ich sehe Jack sowieso am Markt, also kann ich es ihm sagen.)
say.it: **Will you be using the van tomorrow?** Chiedere con garbo dei piani: non chiedi ancora un favore, domandi soltanto. (Domani ti serve il furgone?) Ciò che succederà comunque: **I'll be seeing Jack at the market, so I can tell him.** (Vedrò comunque Jack al mercato, quindi posso dirglielo.)
say.en: **Will you be using the van tomorrow?** A polite question about plans: you aren't asking for it yet, only asking. For what will happen anyway: **I'll be seeing Jack at the market, so I can tell him.**

exercises.text: — What are you doing tomorrow? — I'm ___ (climb) Helvellyn with Jack. — In this weather? Look at those clouds: it ___ (rain)! — I don't think it ___ (last). The bus ___ (leave) at seven, so by nine we'll be on the fell. — Well, this time tomorrow I ___ (sit) by the fire. — ___ you be using the van? — No, I ___ (not need) it. Take it.

translation.sl: — Kaj boš delal{m:|f:a} jutri? — Z Jackom grem na Helvellyn. — V tem vremenu? Poglej te oblake: deževalo bo! — Mislim, da ne bo trajalo. Avtobus odpelje ob sedmih, tako da bova ob devetih na hribu. — No, jutri ob tem času bom sedel{m:|f:a} pri ognju. — Boš rabil{m:|f:a} kombi? — Ne, ne bom ga rabil{m:|f:a}. Vzemi ga.
translation.de: — Was machst du morgen? — Ich gehe mit Jack auf den Helvellyn. — Bei dem Wetter? Schau dir die Wolken an: Es wird gleich regnen! — Ich glaube nicht, dass es lange dauert. Der Bus fährt um sieben, also sind wir um neun am Berg. — Na ja, morgen um diese Zeit sitze ich beim Feuer. — Brauchst du den Lieferwagen? — Nein, ich brauche ihn nicht. Nimm ihn.
translation.it: — Che cosa fai domani? — Salgo sull'Helvellyn con Jack. — Con questo tempo? Guarda quelle nuvole: sta per piovere! — Non credo che durerà. L'autobus parte alle sette, quindi alle nove saremo sul monte. — Be', domani a quest'ora sarò sedut{m:o|f:a} accanto al fuoco. — Ti serve il furgone? — No, non mi serve. Prendilo.
translation.en: — What are you doing tomorrow? — I'm climbing Helvellyn with Jack. — In this weather? Look at those clouds: it is going to rain! — I don't think it will last. The bus leaves at seven, so by nine we'll be on the fell. — Well, this time tomorrow I will be sitting by the fire. — Will you be using the van? — No, I won't need it. Take it.

translation.en: The dance starts at eight: it's on the poster. I will be working at the inn until seven, so I can come. — I'm sure it will be fun! — This time next week we will be dancing. — Look at Sam's van! The wheel is going to come off!
